discussion_comments.comment_body:
importProjectFromJSON only validates the top-level structure before persisting the project. scene.tracks, elements, settings, and timelineViewState are written directly to storage, so a malformed import could be saved successfully and only fail later when the project is opened.

Consider validating the imported project against a schema (e.g. Zod) before calling saveProject rather than relying on presence checks and the as ExportedProjectJSON cast.

Thanks @mikekangdev, good catch. Pushed 30179bf: `importProjectFromJSON` now validates the payload against a Zod schema (scenes → tracks → elements, settings, and timeline view state) before `saveProject`, instead of the top-level presence checks plus the `as ExportedProjectJSON` cast. A malformed file is now rejected up front rather than saved and failing later on open.

Zod was already a dependency in `apps/web`, so no new deps. Unknown/extra fields are tolerated for forward compatibility, and the original parsed object is what gets persisted so no element fields are stripped.
